text:
Maya: quick check — dropped the latest draft here: https://docs.redwood.ai/launchs/rl-inference-post-v3.md. please focus on CTAs, benchmark framing, and the webinar CTA placement. aiming to publish Wed 3/25 10am PT.

Ben: see it — nice flow. a couple of legal-y lines to flag: the latency claims in paragraph 3 need source attribution. can we add the 95th percentile number and link to the internal benchmark table?

Olivia: tagging bench team: @Samira can you confirm the 95p and the model/instance combo used for that stat? we should avoid implying guaranteed SLA.

Samira: I ran the final run yesterday. 95p = 124ms on g5-16 with quantized llama-like model (v1.2). confirm we want to call out "~120ms 95th" or keep it more conservative ("~120-130ms"). also attached short CSV: /s3/bench/launch/95p_run_2026-03-18.csv

Maya: thanks — let's do "~120ms (95th) on g5-16, quantized" — Olivia, does that read ok from a marketing POV?

Olivia: yes, that phrasing is good. add parenthetical: (internal benchmark; workloads vary).

Ben: legal ok with that as long as we link to the benchmark appendix and don't market it as guaranteed. add link to appendix in bottom notes.

Zach: landing hero still needs a quote. Can we use the customer beta line from Jake at Sentra? "Redwood cut inference cost and made latencies predictable for our product" — need permission to publish. @Maya can you confirm sign-off?

Maya: pinged Jake; await OK. if no response by EOD tomorrow we'll use a generic customer paraphrase: "early beta reduced inference cost and stabilized latency" (legal-approved).

Samira: for the benchmark figure in the post, can we include a short 3-row table? snippet: ```Model | Hardware | 95th
LlamaX-7B-q | g5-16 | 124ms``` should be fine.

Olivia: yep, that table is helpful. can we also include a one-line callout under it for how we measured (token length, batch size)? keeps transparency.

Maya: added a small measurement note: "95th measured on 1k requests, median prompt length 64 tokens, batching disabled." LMK if wording needs tightening.

Ben: legal -> add the HubSpot inbound routing note to the ops/CTA section. We can’t promise leads will flow to specific SDRs, but we can show recommended routing: webinar registrants -> Marketing MQL pipeline; benchmark interest -> Product MQLs.

Maya: ok I added CTA mapping. snippet in the draft: ```CTA: Download benchmark kit -> HubSpot form (pipeline: Benchmarks); CTA: Register webinar -> Webinar pipeline (nurture: 7-day drip)```

Samira: quick ops check — can we include a small ask for customers to choose region preference? that'll help routing for Dedicated/Private leads.

Olivia: good call. short line under CTAs: "select preferred region in form (NA/EU/APAC)".

Zach: session asks for webinar — proposed topic: "Reducing inference unit cost with batching & KV cache". I'd like the CTA button to map registrants into the webinar workflow and also flag for a follow-up demo request tag.

Maya: done. added demo-request checkbox on the form that toggles a tag -> HubSpot: demo-request = true. ops to confirm automation.

Samira: ops note: we'll need the webhook mapping and the tag rules. @launch-bot scheduled a quick handoff on Mon 3/23 11am with Ops to validate mappings.

launch-bot: publish-check scheduled: Mon 2026-03-23 11:00 PT — ops handoff meeting created. invite: #marketing-ops.

Ben: legal final: I'll do a quick read tomorrow morning and push any micro-edits inline.

Olivia: i'll do a final copy edit after legal pass, then send to design for hero image and benchmark infographic.

Maya: great — timeline: legal by Tue AM, copy edit Tue afternoon, design Wednesday AM, publish Wed 10am PT. If Jake signs off on the quote we'll include it; otherwise use generic paraphrase. thanks everyone :heart:
